title: Duskrush: a survivors-like made entirely with AI assistance. Free to play in the browser
author: Available-Cover-1211
selftext:
**Play it here:** [https://duskrush.pages.dev](https://duskrush.pages.dev/)

I've been building a survivors-like called **Duskrush** with Claude as my coding partner, and I wanted to share how the process went, since this sub is about developing with AI.

The whole game is one HTML file using Canvas2D, with no engine and no build step. I describe what I want in plain language (a new weapon, a boss pattern, a difficulty curve), Claude writes or patches the code, and I play it and tell it what feels wrong. Most of the design decisions came out of that loop. For example, I had a meteor weapon that players kept confusing with the enemy attack telegraphs, so I asked for it to be replaced, and it became homing wisps instead. Another time I kept dying around 2:30, so we added an intermediate difficulty tier instead of just nerfing everything.

What worked well: fast iteration on balance and content, and having the AI write the boring-but-hard parts (spatial grid for hundreds of enemies, deterministic RNG, save data, a runtime FR/EN translation layer). It also built the Supabase leaderboard and anonymous opt-in analytics, and tested the game with headless-browser scripts.

What didn't work as well: it can't feel the game. Pacing and whether a dodge is satisfying still need a human playing it again and again. I also had to be strict about asking for small, testable changes, because big rewrites broke things.

The game: you survive a 15 minute run against growing hordes, pick up to 3 weapons and 3 passives, dodge telegraphed boss attacks, and unlock new heroes, worlds and curse levels. It's free in the browser.

**Play it here:** [https://duskrush.pages.dev](https://duskrush.pages.dev/)  
(Optional, anonymous stats and a leaderboard are available. Nothing is sent unless you accept.)

I'd love feedback on difficulty, since I tune it by feel. Thanks & Enjoy!
